items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: She had just finished making that all-black western, 'Harlem on the Prairie' with Herb Jefferies

ctx.x: But anyway, I joined Fletcher, went to -- well, we played -- in fact, the personnel of the band then was -- the reed section was Hilton Jefferson and myself, Ben Webster and Elmer Williams. And Pop Smith was the trumpet player, Russell Smith and Dick Vance and Emmett Berry were the trumpet players. And Cuffy and the other trombone player, I can't think of his name, was out of Chicago. Naturally, Fletcher was on piano and we had a fellow named Pete Suggs on drums, Israel Crosby on bass and Larry Lucie on guitar.

Then we played the Grand Terrace in Chicago. And my wife, she was in show business. She had been in Hollywood and made pictures. She had made 23 pictures for Cecil B. DeMille and she had just finished making that all-black western, "Harlem on the Prairie" with Herb Jefferies (inaudible). She was the leading lady in there. Her name was --
